baseline.name: Remember every visited node address
baseline.approach: Insert node addresses in a hash set and report a cycle when one repeats.
baseline.time: Expected O(d) for d distinct reachable nodes

archived.name: Floyd slow/fast pointers
archived.time: O(mu+lambda) for a cyclic list with prefix length mu and cycle length lambda; O(n) for an acyclic list

why: Relative pointer motion detects repetition without retaining the visited set.
quantitative_comparison: The set can store d addresses plus hash metadata. Floyd uses two cursor variables and O(mu+lambda) iterations for a cycle with prefix mu and length lambda. Both have linear growth; no faster-runtime factor is established, and Floyd dereferences more links per iteration.
tradeoffs: The set approach can directly retain the first repeated node. Floyd requires valid stable next pointers and an additional phase if the cycle entry is needed.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
